arxiv-2202-07025.title: Box Supervised Video Segmentation Proposal Network
arxiv-2202-07025.creator: Tanveer Hannan, Rajat Koner *, Jonathan Kobold, Matthias Schubert
arxiv-2202-07025.description: Abstract Video Object Segmentation (VOS) has been targeted by various fully-supervised and self-supervised approaches. While fully-supervised methods demonstrate excellent results, self-supervised ones, which do not use pixel-level ground truth, attract much attention. However, self-supervised approaches pose a significant performance gap.

arxiv-2211-09070.title: Towards Computationally Verifiable Semantic Grounding for Language Models
arxiv-2211-09070.creator: Chris Alberti Kuzman Ganchev Michael Collins
arxiv-2211-09070.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Chris Alberti Kuzman Ganchev Michael Collins. The paper presents an approach to semantic grounding of language models (LMs) that conceptualizes the LM as a conditional model generating text given a desired semantic message formalized as a set of entity-relationship triples. It embeds the LM in an auto-encoder by feeding its output to a semantic parser whose output is in the same representation domain as the input message.

arxiv-2302-11409.description: Abstract . The traditional user-centered design process can hardly keep up with the ever faster technical development and increasingly diverse user preferences. As a solution, we propose to augment the tried-and-tested approach of conducting user studies with simulation and optimization of the entire human-computer interaction loop.

arxiv-2309-13493.title: Structure of the probability mass function of the Poisson distribution of order k k Journal: (internal report CC23-6)
arxiv-2309-13493.creator: S. R. Mane
arxiv-2309-13493.description: Abstract The Poisson distribution of order k k is a special case of a compound Poisson distribution. For k = 1 k=1 it is the standard Poisson distribution. Although its probability mass function (pmf) is known, what is lacking is a visual interpretation, which a sum over terms with factorial denominators does not supply.

arxiv-2312-17255.title: Single-channel speech enhancement using learnable loss mixup
arxiv-2312-17255.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . Generalization remains a major problem in supervised learning of single-channel speech enhancement. In this work, we propose learnable loss mixup (LLM) , a simple and effortless training diagram, to improve the generalization of deep learning-based speech enhancement models. Loss mixup , of which learnable loss mixup is a special variant, optimizes a mixture of the loss functions of random sample pairs to train a model on virtual training data constructed from these pairs of samples.

arxiv-2501-03133.title: Cloudy-Maraston : Integrating nebular continuum and line emission with the Maraston stellar population synthesis models 2025 Cloudy-Maraston : Integrating nebular continuum and line emission with the Maraston stellar population synthesis models – B
arxiv-2501-03133.creator: Sophie L. Newman, Christopher C. Lovell, Claudia Maraston, Mauro Giavalisco, William J. Roper, Aayush Saxena, Aswin P. Vijayan, Stephen M. Wilkins
arxiv-2501-03133.description: Abstract The James Webb Space Telescope has ushered in an era of abundant high-redshift observations of young stellar populations characterized by strong emission lines, motivating us to integrate nebular emission into the new Maraston stellar population model which incorporates the latest Geneva stellar evolutionary tracks for massive stars with rotation.

arxiv-2502-14602.title: Qualitative derivation of a density dependent incompressible Darcy law
arxiv-2502-14602.creator: Danica Basarić, Florian Oschmann, Jiaojiao Pan
arxiv-2502-14602.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Danica Basarić, Florian Oschmann, Jiaojiao Pan. This paper provides the first study of the homogenization of the 3D non-homogeneous incompressible Navier–Stokes system in perforated domains with holes of supercritical size. The diameter of the holes is of order ε α ​ ( 1 < α < 3 ) \varepsilon^{\alpha}\ (1<\alpha<3) , where ε > 0 \varepsilon>0 is a small parameter measuring the mutual distance between the holes.

arxiv-2506-16662.title: Bounded Distance Decoding for Random Lattices
arxiv-2506-16662.creator: Shuhong Gao
arxiv-2506-16662.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shuhong Gao. The current paper investigates the bounded distance decoding (BDD) problem for ensembles of lattices whose generator matrices have i.i.d. We first prove that, for these ensembles, BDD remains NP‑hard in the worst case. Then, we introduce a polynomial‑time algorithm based on singular value decomposition (SVD) and establish—both theoretically and through extensive experiments—that, for a randomly selected lattice from the same ensemble, the algorithm solves BDD with high probability.

arxiv-2512-17929.title: Reinforcement Learning for Monetary Policy Under Macroeconomic Uncertainty: Analyzing Tabular and Function Approximation Methods
arxiv-2512-17929.creator: Sheryl Chen, Tony Wang, Kyle Feinstein
arxiv-2512-17929.description: Abstract We study how a central bank should dynamically set short-term nominal interest rates to stabilize inflation and unemployment when macroeconomic relationships are uncertain and time-varying. We model monetary policy as a sequential decision-making problem where the central bank observes macroeconomic conditions quarterly and chooses interest rate adjustments.

pmc-12464121.title: A nomogram and random forest model for predicting liver metastasis in patients with early-onset colorectal cancer
pmc-12464121.creator: Xingzhi Han, Xueying Bai, Qun Zhang, Xiaoping Qian
pmc-12464121.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The incidence of colorectal cancer (CRC) in individuals under the age of 50 has increased. Liver metastasis (LM) is the most common metastasis in CRC patients and is associated with a poor prognosis. This study aimed to use public databases to identify the risk factors for LM in early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) patients and develop a nomogram to quantify the risk of LM.

pmc-12621137.title: Perinatal nutrition as a key regulator of genomic imprinting: a new paradigm for maternal-child health
pmc-12621137.creator: Lucia Aronica, Samantha N. Fessler, Emily Stone Rydbom, Randy L. Jirtle
pmc-12621137.description: Genomic imprinting, characterized by parent-of-origin specific gene expression, represents a critical molecular bridge between early life exposures and long-term health outcomes. Unlike most epigenetic marks, inherited gametic imprint control regions normally remain stable across tissues and throughout life, making them valuable biomarkers of early environmental influences.

pmc-12696669.title: Multiscale modes of functional brain connectivity
pmc-12696669.creator: S Rezvan Farahibozorg, Samuel J Harrison, Janine D Bijsterbosch, Mark W Woolrich, Stephen M Smith
pmc-12696669.description: Information processing in the brain spans from localised sensorimotor processes to higher-level cognition that integrates across multiple regions. Interactions between and within these subsystems enable multiscale information processing. Despite this multiscale characteristic, functional brain connectivity is often either estimated based on 10–30 distributed modes or parcellations with 100–1000 localised parcels, both missing across-scale functional interactions.

uslaw-usc-t19-s3011.title: 19 U.S.C. § 3011 — Transition to Harmonized Tariff Schedule
uslaw-usc-t19-s3011.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t19-s3011.description: United States Code, Title 19 (Customs Duties); Chapter 18 (Implementation Of Harmonized Tariff Schedule). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Existing executive actions (1) The appropriate officers of the United States Government shall take whatever actions are necessary to conform, to the fullest extent practicable, with the tariff classification system of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule all proclamations, regulations, rulings, notices, findings, determinations.
